findings.title: Task cancellation during start() or run_until_stopped() skips all rollback: lease, started components and runtime stay held
findings.evidence: engine.py start() wraps _startup_sequence in `except Exception`; asyncio.CancelledError is a BaseException, so _startup_failure_cleanup never runs. run_until_stopped() has no cleanup path either, and the supervisor loop catches Exception only. Probe P9: a required component whose start() sleeps, task.cancel() after 0.5 s -> journal ['start:core','start:slow'] with no stop, lifecycle state 'starting', instance_lease_acquired=True, instance_lease_released=False, context_closed=False; a second engine in the same run directory is rejected (HostedApplicationStartupError). Probe P10: cancelling run_until_stopped() on a READY engine leaves state 'ready', runtime and components started, lease not released.
findings.reproduction: uv run --extra mcp python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D4/adversarial_scripts/probe_b.py  (keys P9_cancel_during_startup, P10_cancel_run_until_stopped; output logs/probe_b.out.txt)
findings.impact: Any embedding that cancels the host task (wait_for, TaskGroup, a signal path that cancels instead of requesting shutdown) leaks components (for example an owned OS worker), the instance lease and the health task. The D4 rollback and drain proofs cover only Exception-class failures and the cooperative control path. FRZ-REL-04 (cancellation propagates correctly) is listed for R005.
findings.repair_scope: Handle CancelledError in HostedApplicationEngine.start/run_until_stopped (and the supervisor's finally): run the bounded terminal cleanup under asyncio.shield, then re-raise; add negative tests for cancel during startup, during READY and during stop.

findings.title: The in-flight drain and flush machinery is unreachable from the product host: no product HostedApplicationActiveWorkController and no seam in run_hosted_application
findings.evidence: grep over intergrax/ applications/ agents/ scripts/ finds no implementation of stop_intake/wait_for_idle and no non-test `active_work_controller=` argument. runner._build_engine_factory builds HostedApplicationEngine without active_work_controller or flush_services and run_hosted_application() accepts only a profile and an event publisher factory, so in the product runner active_work_before is always 0 and the DRAIN/CANCEL/FLUSH phases are SKIPPED or empty. The only proofs (tests/qualification/pdc_x/d4/test_xd05_drain_background_work.py and the XD-05 integration) use the test-side AsyncioActiveWork adapter; the XD-05 docstring itself states 'the product ships the port but no implementation'. The LKW hosted runtime stop() only sets uvicorn should_exit and states 'platform engine owns shutdown budget'.
findings.reproduction: grep -rn 'def wait_for_idle\|active_work_controller=' --include=*.py intergrax applications agents scripts ; read intergrax/hosting/runner.py:216-250 and applications/local_workspace_application/hosting/runtime.py:213-226
findings.impact: R005 ('graceful shutdown with in-flight drain') is proven for the engine mechanism with an injected port, not for the product composition; background work of a product host is not drained by the host engine.
findings.repair_scope: Provide a product adapter over the background worker runtime (D7 contract) and a seam in the runner/profile to install an active-work controller and flush services; add a runner-level test that submits work, requests shutdown and asserts drain, cancel and exit class.

findings.title: The OS-process crash proof relies on a test-owned crash detector; the product supervisor is in-process and ships no process watcher
findings.evidence: test_d4_crash_restart_subprocess.py defines _SupervisedWorkerRuntime in the test: its _watch() polls the child Popen and calls control.request_restart('worker_process_exited'). HostedApplicationSupervisor ('In-process hosted application supervisor (APP-HOST-5C)') only restarts on the exit of its own engine; nothing in intergrax/hosting observes an OS child or the host process. The proof therefore shows 'a restart request after a worker death is honoured', not that the product detects a crash. A crash of the host process itself has no product supervisor (R012 OS service adapters are an authorized exclusion).
findings.reproduction: read tests/qualification/pdc_x/d4/test_d4_crash_restart_subprocess.py:50-97 and intergrax/hosting/supervisor/supervisor.py:1-5; mutation M7 (never restart) is killed, so the restart half is real
findings.impact: The R007 wording 'restart supervision with an OS-process crash proof' overstates what the product provides; the claim holds only for applications that bring their own process monitor.
findings.repair_scope: Either narrow the claim to 'supervised restart on a control-plane restart request, proven with an OS worker kill', or add a product component/port that watches an owned child process and requests the restart, plus a crash proof of the host process through an external launcher script.

findings.title: A hung runtime.ready() leaves the readiness snapshot reporting ready indefinitely (stale, no health_evaluation_failed)
findings.evidence: engine._refresh_health awaits self._runtime.ready(context) without a timeout (components have health_timeout_seconds, the runtime does not). Probe F: after READY, ready() made to hang and the runtime marked not started; after 1.5 s and 1.0 s health_snapshot().ready stays True, health_evaluation_failed False, last_evaluated_at unchanged. Shutdown still returns because stop_polling is bounded.
findings.impact: A wedged runtime is advertised as ready and keeps accepting new work (accepting_new_work stays True).
findings.repair_scope: Bound runtime.ready (and the refresh as a whole) with a configurable timeout; on timeout mark_health_evaluation_failed so ready turns False; add a hung-probe test.

findings.title: 'Single effective composition root' does not hold: the lab host factory builds a second tool wiring beside wire_application_environment, and no gate asserts the single root
findings.evidence: applications/lab_application/host/factory.py:225 calls wire_lab_tools() (host/tool_wiring.py -> build_application_tool_wiring with a hard-coded sandbox tenant 'lab') when include_mcp is set and passes that registry to build_lab_mcp_server, independent of the registry produced by wire_application_environment. wire_application_environment also accepts conformance_check=False (skips registry/graph/package/tool conformance) and ProfileInvariantValidator(fail_on_violation=False). The matrix cites host_01, which does not mention wire_application_environment (see F-D4-15); no test or script gate forbids a second composition path.
findings.impact: The tools exposed over MCP by the lab host are not the tools the composition root validated; the 'single root' claim is not enforceable as stated.
findings.repair_scope: Route the lab MCP path through the composition root's tool wiring (or declare and gate the exception); add a gate that product host factories do not call build_application_tool_wiring; document the conformance_check opt-out as lab-only.

findings.verification: CODE_READ_BY_AUDITOR (not reproduced against a live sandbox backend)
findings.title: Composition opens the hosted sandbox session under the fixed tenant 'harness' and task 'bootstrap', whatever tenant_id the host is composed for
findings.evidence: environment_wiring.py:438-448: when no sandbox session is passed and an integration profile exists, resolve_hosted_sandbox_session(..., tenant_id='harness', task_id='bootstrap') is called and the session is handed to build_application_tool_wiring for every tenant. HostedSandboxSession.open is a cloud session. The tenant_id parameter of wire_application_environment is not used for it.
findings.impact: With sandbox_host configured, tenant-specific host composition shares one sandbox identity across tenants (R018 TENANT_IMPACT is HIGH); not verified against a real backend.
findings.repair_scope: Derive the sandbox tenant/task from the composition tenant_id (fail closed when absent) or open the session lazily per tool invocation; add a tenant-isolation test with a fake SandboxHostBackend.

findings.title: The public hosting API fingerprint ignores model_config, validators and Field constraints, so a contract loosening passes the COMPAT gate
findings.evidence: describe_public_symbol() records bases, own public member signatures and model field annotation/required only. Probe P2: two pydantic models with the same field annotation but (extra=forbid, ge=1, le=5, frozen) versus (extra=allow, ge=-100, le=500) get an identical fingerprint; flipping HostedApplicationProfile.model_config['extra'] from 'forbid' to 'allow' leaves its fingerprint unchanged. This is the exact class of change made to HostDeploymentProfile in the same wave (F-D4-10). Positive: structural changes are caught (mutation M8, a new public method, is killed).
findings.reproduction: uv run --extra mcp python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D4/adversarial_scripts/probe_a.py  (keys P2_*; output logs/probe_a.out.txt)
findings.impact: HOSTING_PUBLIC_API_VERSION=1.0.0 does not guarantee behavioural stability of public models (strictness, bounds, cross-field validators).
findings.repair_scope: Include model_config, field constraints (metadata) and validator names in describe_public_symbol; regenerate the manifest with a new version entry; add a test that loosening extra/bounds changes the fingerprint.

findings.title: TL-FIX-C is closed only for the three lkw_* keys: business_agents_deploy_enabled stays typed on the generic profile, the LKW vocabulary moved into a platform-tier module, and the guard vocabulary cannot see the remaining key
findings.evidence: The architecture table TIER3_APPLICATION_ENVIRONMENT.md:179-182 lists four keys as product-owned (lkw_hybrid_daemon_enabled, lkw_daemon_bind_host, lkw_daemon_port, business_agents_deploy_enabled). B-D4 moved three; sub_profiles.py:517 still declares business_agents_deploy_enabled, consumed by intergrax/applications/_shared/business_agent_deploy_wiring.py and enabled by the product preset (presets.py:342). The new LkwHybridDaemonDeployment model lives in intergrax/applications/_shared/lkw_hybrid_daemon_wiring.py (platform tier), while the plan row 129 requires 'application-owned or typed extension-owned' configuration. test_d4_no_product_vocabulary.py uses PRODUCT_VOCABULARY=('lkw','daemon','local_workspace',...), which by construction cannot flag 'business_agents'.
findings.impact: R015 is at best partially closed by the repository's own TL-FIX-C definition; a regression test would pass although a documented product key remains.
findings.repair_scope: Decide ownership of business_agents_deploy_enabled (move to a product/extension-owned model or record it as platform vocabulary with an ADR note); move LkwHybridDaemonDeployment under applications/local_workspace_application or a declared typed extension; align the guard vocabulary with the table.

findings.title: Documentation status is stale after B-D4: TL-FIX-C still 'ACCEPTED / PLANNED / not fixed' in the architecture and the plan; APP-CON-8 'Done' rows in the satellite plan carry no isolation bound
findings.evidence: TIER3_APPLICATION_ENVIRONMENT.md (architecture) lines 27, 47, 171-173, 273, 282, 297, 601, 619 and the plan row at plans/TIER3_APPLICATION_ENVIRONMENT.md:129 still describe TL-FIX-C as planned/not fixed and 'A4, not A5 while TL-FIX-C remains accepted'. The same wave reconciled TL-FIX-D (R016, a freeze-blocker row) for exactly this plan/code mismatch. For R019 the bounded claim ('not a universal production isolation guarantee') is present in the architecture (lines 271, 561) and in the main plan row (plans/TIER3...:71-74) but not in the satellite plans/satellites/TIER3_APPLICATION_ENVIRONMENT_embedded_detail.md rows 11, 12, 60 which mark shadow/sandbox lifecycle 'Done'.
findings.impact: FRZ-DOC-01 style plan/code mismatch re-introduced; readers get contradictory maturity statements (A4 vs implemented).
findings.repair_scope: After F-D4-08 is decided, update status rows, the A-level text and the key table in architecture and plan; add the isolation bound (or a pointer) to the three satellite rows.

findings.title: HostDeploymentProfile changed from extra='forbid' to extra='allow': typos in generic keys are silently accepted and a non-loopback bind host is not constrained
findings.evidence: Probe P1: HostDeploymentProfile(business_agents_deploy_enabld=True) is accepted into model_extra while the typed flag stays False; LkwHybridDaemonDeployment.from_host_deployment accepts lkw_daemon_bind_host='0.0.0.0'; a misspelled lkw_ key (lkw_daemon_prot) and nested values are rejected. The previous model (git show 145b49bad^) was extra='forbid' but also had no bind-host validator, so the wide bind is not a regression. test_r015_generic_profile_accepts_only_flat_scalar_product_keys pins the new permissive behaviour.
findings.impact: A mistyped deployment switch is ignored without diagnostics; a daemon can be bound to all interfaces by configuration (default stays 127.0.0.1).
findings.repair_scope: Require product-owned keys to match a registered prefix and fail on unknown unprefixed keys (or expose a typed extension registry); validate bind_host against loopback unless an explicit opt-in flag is set.

findings.title: Instance guard: stale lock metadata whose PID now belongs to an unrelated live process rejects a legitimate start (PID reuse)
findings.evidence: file_guard._classify_prior_metadata raises 'live_process_metadata' when prior.process_id is alive, although the exclusive OS lock was acquired (so the prior owner no longer holds it); process_started_at is stored but never compared. Probe P3: lock file with metadata of pid=<this live pid>, started_at=2020, no lock held -> acquire() raises HostedApplicationInstanceConflictError (reason live_process_metadata). Positive: probe D (hard-kill of the real lease holder process) -> a new engine starts READY with hosting.instance.stale_recovered.
findings.reproduction: uv run --extra mcp python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D4/adversarial_scripts/probe_a.py (P3) and probe_d.py
findings.impact: After a crash on a host with fast PID reuse (Windows) the restart can be refused until the metadata file is removed manually; fail-closed, no safety violation.
findings.repair_scope: Treat metadata as live only if both pid and process_started_at match the live process; add a PID-reuse test with a fake probe.

findings.title: Downstream event/metric publishes are awaited without a bound in the shutdown path (engine and supervisor)
findings.evidence: engine._publish_metric awaits the dispatcher directly; _graceful_stop_sequence also awaits the APPLICATION_STOPPING publish and _publish_exit_class_metric outside run_bounded_phase (only the terminal stopped event is bounded). HostingEventDispatcher.publish awaits the downstream publisher with no timeout, and the observability export policy has no timeout. The supervisor's _publish_metric_safe and _publish_restart_event_safe are equally unbounded. Probe P11: a publisher that hangs on the drain_duration metric -> engine.stop() did not return within 60 s (computed budget 150 s; every bounded phase finished in < 1 s).
findings.impact: A hanging exporter or custom publisher can block shutdown and restart past the declared budget.
findings.repair_scope: Publish through run_bounded_phase/asyncio.wait_for using the observer timeout in the engine and supervisor; record a secondary failure on timeout; add a hanging-publisher test.

findings.title: Lifecycle metrics are exported only when the host enables an observability policy; the product runner default exports nothing, and the bridge test covers 3 of 6 metrics
findings.evidence: run_hosted_application() defaults to ObservabilityHostedApplicationEventPublisher() whose ObservabilityExportPolicy is enabled=False. Probe P6: all six metric events published through a default publisher produce 0 exported envelopes; with enabled=True all six survive with name and label (probe P5). test_r009_metrics_reach_the_canonical_observability_export_bridge asserts only start, ready, drain_duration. No test composes the product runner with an enabled exporter.
findings.reproduction: uv run --extra mcp python docs/project/maintainers/qualification/iiac_evidence/PDC-X/D4/adversarial_scripts/probe_a.py  (keys P5_*, P6_*)
findings.impact: R009 holds at the event-port level; a default product host emits the events but exports no metric until the operator wires an exporter.
findings.repair_scope: Assert all six metrics through the bridge; add a runner-level test with an enabled InMemory exporter; document the opt-in in the hosting architecture.

findings.title: The D4 qualification suites and host_01 are not wired into any CI workflow, regression profile or ENT-AUDIT impact rule
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/*.yml run tests/unit (-m 'gate and not no_ci'), ent_audit_x and diagnostics suites only; no workflow or scripts/ci/run_regression_gate_ci.py profile references tests/qualification/pdc_x/d4 or tests/qualification/host_01. The ENT-AUDIT impact map maps intergrax/hosting to ENT-A-* structural checks, none of which runs the D4 suite or the public-API gate (PDC_TIER3_ROOT_IMPACT_RULES covers the root applications/ prefix only, as intended by T-IGX-040-A).
findings.impact: The R014 version gate and the lifecycle regressions are protected only when a person replays the campaign suites.
findings.repair_scope: Add the D4 directory (or the public-API test) to the smoke/enterprise regression profile and a hosting impact rule that selects it.

findings.title: The cited evidence 'host_01' does not exercise R001 or R002 (the closed-world inventory itself labels it 'execution boundary only')
findings.evidence: grep -c over tests/qualification/host_01/*.py for HostedApplicationProfile, ApplicationEnvironmentProfile and wire_application_environment returns 0 in every file; HOST-Q1..Q12 cover the task execution port, root launcher, error mapping and transport purity. R001 is independently supported by tests/unit/hosting/test_hosted_application_profile*.py (passed) and tests/unit/applications/test_environment_profile.py (passed); R002 has no direct gate (see F-D4-05).
findings.impact: 'Closure via PDC-P7-D4 replay of host_01' cannot evidence these two rows; the matrix EVIDENCE_PATH is generic for every D4 row.
findings.repair_scope: Map R001 to the hosting profile and environment profile suites and add a single-root gate for R002; correct the matrix TEST_CASE.

findings.title: run_bounded_phase is cooperative: work that swallows cancellation overruns its limit and is still reported COMPLETED
findings.evidence: Probe P7: limit 0.2 s, work that sleeps 2 s inside `except CancelledError` -> outcome 'completed' after 2.22 s. A TimeoutError raised by the work itself is also classified TIMED_OUT.
findings.impact: The 'bounded shutdown' guarantee depends on well-behaved controllers/components; a stubborn one defeats the budget silently.
findings.repair_scope: Document the cooperative contract; optionally race the phase against a deadline with asyncio.wait and abandon the task, recording FORCED.

findings.title: Dossier F-13 confirmed at this SHA but it is not a D4 requirement row: queue recovery redelivers crash-interrupted tasks while the worker passes idempotency_store=None
findings.evidence: intergrax/queueing/providers/document_store/colocated_worker.py:83-86 (recover_interrupted_running with the RetryPolicy budget) and :141 (idempotency_store=None); document_store_task_queue.recover_interrupted_running settles against the budget instead of FAILED when max_retries is set. Owner is the queueing/background domain.
findings.reproduction: read the two files at the cited lines
findings.impact: Opt-in at-least-once redelivery without an idempotency ledger can double-run side effects (default without a policy keeps FAILED).
findings.repair_scope: Route to the owner of intergrax/queueing (D7); not repaired under D4.

findings.title: Dossier F-41 (impact-map root applications/ rule, T-IGX-040-A) and F-49 (openai catalog dispatch) are outside the D4 rows
findings.evidence: PDC_TIER3_ROOT_IMPACT_RULES (impact_map.py:203-224) matches only paths under the root applications/ prefix and repeats existing ENT-A ids; no D4 row owns a root-applications path in its write set, and the D4 owner paths are under intergrax/hosting and intergrax/applications (mapped by their own prefixes). F-49 concerns intergrax/integrations catalog dispatch, not hosting or environment composition. Both were therefore not judged as D4 defects; F-D4-14 notes that the impact map selects no D4 suite.
findings.impact: None for D4.
findings.repair_scope: None under D4.

findings.title: Environment and out-of-row red tests observed during the audit
findings.evidence: (a) A clean worktree .venv (default groups test+quality) lacks fastmcp: tests/qualification/host_01 fails at collection until `--extra mcp` is used; psycopg is absent (4 tests in tests/unit/applications/architecture fail with IntegrationConfigurationError; a fifth, test_npsc1_*, fails with OrchestrationGovernanceEvidenceCompositionError 'requires governance_evidence_persistence'). (b) 3 tests in tests/unit/hosting/instance (symlink rejection) fail with WinError 1314 (no symlink privilege) instead of skipping. (c) tests/unit/applications/test_package_wiring.py::test_strict_product_package_closure_passes (marked no_ci) fails with MemoryProviderAdmissionError qualification_evidence_missing (fail-closed: no evidence registry is passed); two further architecture gates are stale (test_gr10_r10_r2_missing_generic_production_policy_still_fail_closed patches a removed attribute; test_npsc3g_worker_runtime_uses_host_execution asserts text no longer in nexus_worker_execution.py). None of these was compared with the activation pin; none is in a D4 row.
findings.impact: Replays on a clean Windows checkout need the mcp and postgresql extras and symlink privilege; stale gates add noise to unit runs.
findings.repair_scope: Document the extras in the gate runbook, make the symlink tests skip when privilege is missing, retarget or retire the stale gates (owners outside D4).

findings.title: R010 semantics: restart never re-resolves configuration; the digest check compares the engine definition's stored digest strings
findings.evidence: HostedApplicationSupervisor holds one immutable definition and _verify_engine_contract compares engine.definition.profile_digest/definition_digest with it. The digest covers application_factory_id (a string), not the callable. The check rejects an engine composed from a different definition (mutation M5 killed) but cannot detect an engine whose definition object was built from the same digest with different code.
findings.impact: 'Restart preserves configuration' means 'the supervisor refuses a mismatching definition digest', which is what the test proves.
findings.repair_scope: None required; keep the wording of R010 aligned with this semantics.
